findings.title: No removable-media replication observed; drive-letter and USB-related hits are OS/DFS artifacts
findings.summary: Hunting for T1091 (Replication Through Removable Media) across windows.sysmon, windows.security, windows.powershell and windows.other (2020-05-02 02:55–03:28Z, hosts scranton/newyork/nashua/utica.dmevals.local) produced no evidence of removable-media staging or execution. The only non-C: file writes were DFSR replication metadata on newyork.dmevals.local (F:\System Volume Information\DFSR\Config\*.XML.TMP written by C:\windows\system32\DFSRs.exe, recurring ~every 5 minutes) and a D:\pagefile.sys write by smss.exe on scranton.dmevals.local — both normal OS behaviour, not removable media. No process executed from a removable drive, no USBSTOR/removable-device registry artifacts, and no autorun.inf creation were found. The 'autorun' file hits were Sysinternals Autoruns binaries extracted to C:\Users\pbeesly\Downloads\SysinternalsSuite\ by powershell.exe on scranton.dmevals.local, i.e. tooling download, not media-based replication. The MountPoints2 registry writes on scranton.dmevals.local were made by C:\windows\Explorer.EXE (SYSTEM) for volume bookkeeping. The 8 windows.other hits (event.code 2004/2006) were Windows Defender Firewall rule add/delete churn by svchost.exe for 'Usermode Font Driver Host' and 'WARP_JIT_*' rules — unrelated to removable media. Separately noted (outside T1091): the same scranton host shows PsExec64.exe with plaintext credentials targeting \\NASHUA and PSEXESVC service installs on nashua.dmevals.local, which is network-based lateral movement, not removable-media replication.

findings.title: PsExec-style remote service execution on nashua.dmevals.local (PSEXESVC) launching an unsigned python.exe from C:\Windows\Temp
findings.summary: On 2020-05-02 between 03:11:39 and 03:15:03 UTC, four PSEXESVC services were installed on nashua.dmevals.local by user pbeesly (event 7045, Service File Name %SystemRoot%\PSEXESVC.exe, LocalSystem, demand start). Each service start spawned C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe (Sysmon event 1, parent PSEXESVC, user DMEVALS\pbeesly, no FileVersion/Description/Company/OriginalFileName) at 03:11:40, 03:12:46, 03:13:49 and 03:15:03. The python.exe process then made repeated outbound TCP connections from 10.0.1.6 to 192.168.0.4:8443 (e.g. 03:15:05). This is remote service abuse (SMB service creation) used to execute an attacker-supplied binary on a remote host, i.e. exploitation/abuse of a remote service for lateral movement. The same pbeesly account also performed network (type 3) logons to nashua.dmevals.local from 10.0.1.4 and to newyork.dmevals.local from 10.0.1.4, and an RDP (type 10) logon to scranton.dmevals.local from 172.18.39.2 at 03:20:46 UTC, consistent with a compromised account being used to move across hosts.

findings.title: No RDP session hijacking (tscon/session takeover) on any host
findings.summary: The two LogonType 10 events in the dataset are both on scranton.dmevals.local for account pbeesly from 172.18.39.2 at 2020-05-02T03:20:46Z (one non-elevated, one elevated token), immediately preceded by the inbound 3389 connection to TermService and followed by rdpclip.exe (PID 5300, TerminalSessionId 2, parent svchost.exe -k NetworkService -s TermService) — the normal birth of a new RDP session, not the hijack of an existing one. Hijack indicators are absent: no tscon.exe, qwinsta.exe, 'query session' or mstsc.exe process creation in sysmon (only rdpclip.exe matched), no matching PowerShell script blocks, no 4778/4779 session reconnect/disconnect events, and no outbound 3389 connections from any host (the single 3389 record is inbound). The 4648 on scranton targets 'localhost' via svchost.exe, consistent with the local RDP logon itself.

findings.title: PsExec used from SCRANTON to copy PSEXESVC.exe and python.exe to NASHUA over ADMIN$
findings.summary: On 2020-05-02 between 03:10 and 03:18 UTC, user DMEVALS\pbeesly on scranton.dmevals.local (10.0.1.4) repeatedly launched C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\PsExec64.exe from a PowerShell parent with the command line "PsExec64.exe" -accepteula \\NASHUA -u dmevals\pbeesly -p Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by -i 2 C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe (four executions: 03:11:18, 03:12:25, 03:13:28, 03:14:42). The tool transfer is visible on the target: C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe was created on nashua.dmevals.local at 03:10:23 by the System process (SMB write), and Security 5145 events on NASHUA show pbeesly from source 10.0.1.4 writing PSEXESVC.exe to the ADMIN$ share (\\*\ADMIN$, Share Path \\??\C:\windows) with WriteData/AppendData access at 03:13:28 and 03:14:42, plus svcctl and PSEXESVC-SCRANTON-<pid>-stdin/stdout/stderr named-pipe access on IPC$. Each round trip produced a PSEXESVC service install (7045) on NASHUA and a C:\Windows\PSEXESVC.exe file creation, followed by C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe executing as pbeesly with parent C:\Windows\PSEXESVC.exe (03:11:40, 03:12:46, 03:13:49, 03:15:03). The transferred python.exe is a PyInstaller bundle (extracts _MEI29522 with _socket.pyd, _ssl.pyd, _hashlib.pyd at 03:15:04), i.e. a portable tool staged and executed remotely. This is a textbook lateral tool transfer: binaries copied to the remote host's ADMIN$ share and executed via a service. The plaintext password in the command line and the repeated re-copying indicate hands-on-keyboard adversary activity, not administration.

findings.title: Routine SYSVOL/IPC$/ADMIN$ share access by machine accounts and WEC is benign domain traffic
findings.summary: The 42 Security 5140 share-access events and the bulk of the 121 5145 detailed-share events are ordinary domain operations: NEWYORK$ accessing \\*\SYSVOL (Share Path \\??\F:\SYSVOL\sysvol) over its own link-local IPv6 address, and machine accounts SCRANTON$ (10.0.1.4), NASHUA$ (10.0.1.6), UTICA$ (10.0.1.5) and WEC$ (10.0.1.10) touching \\*\IPC$ for samr/lsarpc RPC endpoints. These are domain-controller replication, Group Policy and Windows Event Collector traffic, not tool staging. The only ADMIN$ writes in the dataset are the pbeesly/PSEXESVC.exe transfers to NASHUA described in the malicious finding. The Zeek smb_files records (2020-04-30, non-overlapping window) show SMB file activity from 10.0.1.4 and 10.0.1.6 to 10.0.0.4 but carry no file names or hashes in the returned fields, so they cannot be tied to this transfer and are not cited as evidence of it.

T1021.reason: Remote services used for lateral movement: PsExec over SMB/ADMIN$ and WinRM from SCRANTON (10.0.1.4) to NASHUA (10.0.1.6) by pbeesly with cleartext credentials.

T1021.001.reason: Only RDP logon in the data: type 10 for pbeesly on SCRANTON from 172.18.39.2 at 23:20:46, after the PsExec activity; no mstsc.exe or outbound 3389 from a compromised host, so pivot direction is unconfirmed.

T1021.002.reason: Four PSEXESVC service installs on NASHUA, nine ADMIN$ share accesses by pbeesly from 10.0.1.4, PSEXESVC.exe launching C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe, and 4648 explicit-credential logons via PSEXESVC.exe.

T1021.003.reason: 10016 events are local LRPC COM permission failures for SYSTEM/pbeesly; no DCOM remote activation, MMC20.Application or ShellBrowserWindow script blocks.

T1021.004.reason: No ssh.exe/plink/putty executions, no port 22 connections in Sysmon or Zeek, no SSH script blocks.

T1021.005.reason: No VNC binaries, no port 5900 connections in Sysmon or Zeek, no VNC script blocks.

T1021.006.reason: Invoke-Command -ComputerName NASHUA executed by pbeesly on SCRANTON, with powershell.exe opening four connections to 10.0.1.6:5985 and matching inbound connections on NASHUA.

T1072.reason: No software deployment tooling was used. The lateral movement scranton->nashua was carried out with PsExec64.exe (PSEXESVC service installs, 7045) and PowerShell Invoke-Command/Invoke-SeaDukeStage, not SCCM/Intune/WSUS. Checks C052 (SCCM/Intune script blocks), C053 and C054 (ccmexec/Intune/SMS binaries) returned zero hits, and the only management-port network flows (C055) were generic 10.0.1.4 web traffic on 80/443 with no 8530/8531 WSUS/SCCM traffic. The activity itself is malicious lateral movement, but it belongs to T1569.002/T1021.002 rather than T1072.

T1080.reason: pbeesly on scranton (10.0.1.4) wrote Temp\python.exe to \\nashua\ADMIN$ with AccessMask 0x2 (WriteData/AddFile) at 03:10:23, then ran PsExec64.exe against \\NASHUA with the plaintext password to execute C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe, which nashua spawned under C:\Windows\PSEXESVC.exe four times. The share write tainted content executed on another host. Remaining share hits (SYSVOL/IPC$ machine-account GPO reads, svchost GroupPolicy DataStore cache writes, zeek SMB::FILE_OPEN reads of sysvol) are benign.

T1091.reason: No removable-media activity: no execution or file writes from removable drives, no USBSTOR/removable-device registry artifacts, no autorun.inf. The only non-C: writes were DFSR replication metadata on F: (DFSRs.exe) and D:\pagefile.sys (smss.exe); 'autorun' hits were Sysinternals Autoruns binaries in C:\Users\pbeesly\Downloads; MountPoints2 writes came from Explorer.EXE; the 2004/2006 hits were Defender Firewall rule churn by svchost.exe. Lateral movement in this window was network-based (PsExec64 to \\NASHUA, PSEXESVC service installs), not via removable media.

T1210.reason: Remote service abuse observed: PSEXESVC services installed on nashua.dmevals.local by pbeesly spawned an unsigned C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe four times, which then beaconed to 192.168.0.4:8443; accompanied by pbeesly network/RDP logons across nashua, newyork and scranton and an encoded IEX-from-bitmap PowerShell payload on scranton.

T1534.reason: A malicious .scr delivered into pbeesly's session on scranton (launched by explorer.exe) led to a PowerShell stager and UAC bypass; the same pbeesly session then initiated WinRM (10.0.1.4 -> 10.0.1.6:5985) to nashua, where pbeesly network logons, interactive PowerShell, Rar.exe archiving and four PSEXESVC service installs occurred, and authenticated to newyork — internal delivery plus session reuse for lateral movement.

T1550.reason: PsExec64.exe on scranton.dmevals.local launched five times with explicit dmevals\pbeesly credentials against \\NASHUA, producing 4648 cifs/NASHUA logons, PSEXESVC service installs and C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe execution on nashua.dmevals.local.

T1550.002.reason: Only one NTLM network logon exists (pbeesly on scranton, NTLM V2, paired with LogonType 10 sessions from 172.18.39.2); the lateral movement used explicit plaintext credentials, not hash reuse.

T1550.003.reason: Kerberos logons are machine-account/peer traffic with per-session LogonGuids, PreAuthType is unpopulated, and no ticket-related PowerShell script blocks (Rubeus/kirbi/ticket) were found.

T1563.reason: Only remote-service activity is a legitimate inbound RDP session on scranton.dmevals.local (listener start 03:19:11, inbound 3389 from 172.18.39.2, LogonType 10 for pbeesly, rdpclip child of TermService). No session hijacking tooling or reconnect events; PsExec service installs on nashua are remote execution, not session hijacking.

T1563.002.reason: No tscon/qwinsta/'query session'/mstsc execution in sysmon or PowerShell, no 4778/4779 events, no outbound 3389. The two Type 10 logons are a new RDP session for pbeesly on scranton preceded by the inbound 3389 connection, not a takeover of an existing session.

T1570.reason: pbeesly on SCRANTON ran PsExec64.exe four times against \\NASHUA with plaintext credentials to execute C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe; NASHUA shows python.exe created at 03:10:23, PSEXESVC.exe written to the ADMIN$ share from 10.0.1.4 (5145, WriteData), PSEXESVC service installs (7045) and python.exe spawning under C:\Windows\PSEXESVC.exe — a clear lateral tool transfer and remote execution chain.
